source_refs.note: Book p. 160-161 (PDF 162-163): slopes of the lines of ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0, m1 + m2, m1 m2, tan(theta) = 2 sqrt(h^2 - ab)/(a + b), Special Cases, Example 17

blocks.title: Ustad ki baat
blocks.text: Pichhle page par humne seekha ke \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) origin se guzarne wali do lines hain. Ab sawal yeh hai: in dono lines ke darmiyan angle kitna hai? Ek tareeqa yeh hai ke pehle dono lines alag karein, phir slopes nikal kar angle. Lekin aaj hum aisa formula banayenge jo seedha \(a\), \(h\), \(b\) se angle de de, lines alag kiye baghair. Is mein teen purane auzaar kaam aayenge: line ka slope, do lines ke darmiyan angle ka formula (Section 5.6), aur slopes ka jama aur product. Aakhir mein do khaas haalatein dekhenge: lines kab coincident hoti hain aur kab perpendicular.

\[ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0 \quad \text{...(i)}\]
Hum dekh chuke hain ke (i) jin lines ko represent karti hai woh yeh hain:
\[by + x\left(h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0 \quad \text{...(ii)}\]
aur
\[by + x\left(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right) = 0 \quad \text{...(iii)}\]

Ab (ii) aur (iii) ke slopes, bil-tarteeb (respectively), yeh hain:
\[m_{1} = \dfrac{-\left(h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right)}{b}\]
aur
\[m_{2} = \dfrac{-\left(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\right)}{b}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Yeh slopes kahan se aaye? Line \(by + cx = 0\) ko \(y\) ke liye hal karein to \(y = -\frac{c}{b}x\), yani slope \(-c/b\). Line (ii) mein \(x\) ke saath \(c = h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\) hai aur line (iii) mein \(c = h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}\). Bas yahi rakh diya. (Theorem 8 ki tarah yahan bhi \(b \ne 0\) hai, warna \(b\) se divide nahi ho sakta.)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Jama karte waqt square roots aapas mein cancel ho jate hain (ek plus, ek minus), to \(m_{1} + m_{2} = \dfrac{-2h}{b}\).
Multiply karte waqt \((h + \sqrt{h^{2}-ab})(h - \sqrt{h^{2}-ab}) = h^{2} - (h^{2} - ab) = ab\) banta hai, yani \((p + q)(p - q) = p^{2} - q^{2}\) wala formula. Phir \(\dfrac{ab}{b^{2}} = \dfrac{a}{b}\).
Kamaal ki baat: slopes ka jama aur product seedha coefficients se mil gaya. Bilkul waise hi jaise quadratic equation ke roots ka jama \(-B/A\) aur product \(C/A\) hota hai.

Agar \(\theta\) lines (ii) aur (iii) ke darmiyan angle ki measure ho, to
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_{1} - m_{2}}{1 + m_{1}m_{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{(m_{1}+m_{2})^{2} - 4m_{1}m_{2}}}{1 + m_{1}m_{2}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{4h^{2}}{b^{2}} - \dfrac{4a}{b}}}{1 + \dfrac{a}{b}}\]
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b} \quad \text{...(iv)}\]

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
Pehli line mein Section 5.6 ka angle wala formula hai: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{m_{1} - m_{2}}{1 + m_{1}m_{2}}\).
Doosri line mein identity \((m_{1} - m_{2})^{2} = (m_{1} + m_{2})^{2} - 4m_{1}m_{2}\) lagayi. Faida: ab humein \(m_{1}\) aur \(m_{2}\) alag alag nahi chahiye, sirf un ka jama aur product, jo hum ke paas pehle se hain.
Teesri line mein jama aur product rakh diye. Chauthi line mein \(\sqrt{\frac{4h^{2} - 4ab}{b^{2}}} = \frac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{b}\) aur \(1 + \frac{a}{b} = \frac{a + b}{b}\); upar neeche ka \(b\) cancel ho gaya.
Sign ka masla: do lines jab ek doosre ko kaatti hain to do angle bante hain, \(\theta\) aur \(180^{\circ} - \theta\), jaise kainchi ke do phal. Agar (iv) negative jawab de to \(\theta\) obtuse (90 se bada) hai, aur acute angle \(180^{\circ} - \theta\) hai, yani absolute value ka \(\tan^{-1}\).
Is tarah equation (iv) equation (i) ki lines ke darmiyan angle deti hai.

items: Agar dono lines parallel hon to \(\theta = 0\), is liye \(\tan\theta = 0\), jis ka matlab \(h^{2} - ab = 0\). Yahi lines ke coincident hone ki shart hai (origin se guzarne wali do parallel lines lazmi ek hi line hoti hain).
Agar lines perpendicular (ek doosre par amood) hon to \(\theta = 90^{\circ}\), aur \(\tan 90^{\circ}\) defined nahi. Is ka matlab denominator zero hai: \(a + b = 0\).

blocks.text: Lehaza (i) ke perpendicular lines ka jora hone ki shart yeh hai ke \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients ka jama zero ho.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Perpendicular wali shart formula ke baghair bhi samajh aati hai: do lines perpendicular hon to \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\). Aur hum jaante hain \(m_{1}m_{2} = a/b\). To \(a/b = -1\), yani \(a = -b\), yani \(a + b = 0\). Misaal: \(3x^{2} - 8xy - 3y^{2} = 0\) mein \(a + b = 3 - 3 = 0\), is liye is ki dono lines aapas mein perpendicular hain, aik nazar mein!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text:
\(x^{2} - 2xy + y^{2} = 0\) ki lines ke darmiyan angle kitna hai?
Jawab: \(a = 1\), \(h = -1\), \(b = 1\); \(h^{2} - ab = 0\), to \(\tan\theta = 0\), \(\theta = 0^{\circ}\). Waqai yeh \((x - y)^{2} = 0\) hai, ek hi line do dafa.

blocks.title: Example 17
blocks.problem: Find measure of the angle between the lines represented by: \(5x^{2} + 6xy + y^{2} = 0\).
steps:
Diya gaya: \(5x^{2} + 6xy + y^{2} = 0\).
Maloom karna: dono lines ke darmiyan angle \(\theta\).
Tareeqa: equation ko \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) se mila kar \(a\), \(h\), \(b\) parhenge aur formula (iv) lagayenge: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b}\). Yeh formula is liye chuna ke yeh lines ko alag kiye baghair seedha angle de deta hai; waqt bhi bachta hai aur ghalti ka imkaan bhi kam.

\(a\), \(h\), \(b\) parhein
\[a = 5,\quad 2h = 6 \Rightarrow h = 3,\quad b = 1\]
Kyun: \(a\) \(x^{2}\) ka coefficient, \(b\) \(y^{2}\) ka, aur \(h\) \(xy\) ke coefficient ka aadha hai.
Dhyan dein: \(h = 6\) le liya to \(h^{2} - ab = 31\) ban jayega aur jawab ghalat. Aadha lena mat bhooliye.

Square root ka hisaab
\[h^{2} - ab = 9 - 5 = 4\]
\[\sqrt{h^{2} - ab} = 2\]
Kyun: \(h^{2} - ab\) positive aaya, matlab Theorem 8 ke mutabiq lines real aur alag hain, is liye un ke darmiyan angle maujood hai.

Formula (iv) lagayein
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{9 - 5}}{5 + 1} = \dfrac{2(2)}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\]
Kyun: numerator mein \(2 \times 2 = 4\) aur denominator mein \(a + b = 6\); \(4/6\) ko simplify kar ke \(2/3\).

Angle nikalein
\[\theta = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{3}\right) = 33.69^{\circ}\]
Kyun: \(\tan\theta\) positive hai, is liye \(\theta\) acute (90 se chhota) hai. Calculator ko degree mode mein rakh kar \(\tan^{-1}\) dabaiye.

Tasdeeq:
\[5x^{2} + 6xy + y^{2} = (5x + y)(x + y)\]
\[m_{1} = -5,\quad m_{2} = -1\]
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{-1 - (-5)}{1 + 5} = \dfrac{4}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: lines alag kar ke purane slope wale formula se bhi wahi jawab aaya, to hamara hisaab pakka hai.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
Negative jawab wali haalat dekhiye: \(2x^{2} + 5xy - 3y^{2} = 0\). Yahan \(a = 2\), \(h = 5/2\), \(b = -3\).
\[h^{2} - ab = \dfrac{25}{4} + 6 = \dfrac{49}{4}\]
\[\tan\theta = \dfrac{2(7/2)}{2 - 3} = -7\]
Negative aaya, to yeh obtuse angle \(98.13^{\circ}\) hai. Acute angle \(180^{\circ} - 98.13^{\circ} = 81.87^{\circ}\), yani \(\tan^{-1} 7\). Ghabraiye mat, dono jawab ek hi jore ke do angle hain.

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. \(ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} = 0\) ke liye: \(m_{1} + m_{2} = -2h/b\), \(m_{1}m_{2} = a/b\).
2. Angle: \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^{2}-ab}}{a + b}\).
3. Coincident (angle zero): \(h^{2} = ab\).
4. Perpendicular (angle \(90^{\circ}\)): \(a + b = 0\), yani \(x^{2}\) aur \(y^{2}\) ke coefficients ka jama zero.
5. \(\tan\theta\) negative aaye to angle obtuse hai; acute angle \(180^{\circ}\) mein se minus kar ke.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. \(xy\) ka poora coefficient \(h\) le lena, ya denominator mein \(a + b\) ki jagah \(a - b\) likh dena.
2. Calculator radian mode mein hona: \(\tan^{-1}(2/3) = 0.588\) radians hai, degrees nahi.
3. Perpendicular ki shart \(a = b\) samajh lena; sahi shart \(a + b = 0\) hai.
